items.title: SpaceX proposes a $24 billion Texas supercomputer worth 17 times its bitcoin pile
items.summary: The $24 billion project, which includes an AI supercomputer in Texas with its own gas-fired power plant, is about 17 times the value of SpaceX's bitcoin holdings.

items.title: Solana moves to scrap the transaction feature used in the $270 million Drift hack
items.summary: A draft proposal would end the 'durable nonces' feature no earlier than May 5, 2027, forcing custodians that sign offline to rebuild how they move coins.

items.title: Two rival Ethereum proposals aim to stop Glamsterdam breaking old contracts
items.summary: The proposals aim to keep Ethereum’s planned gas changes from breaking existing contracts, using different approaches to what contracts see and what users pay.

items.title: Binance's bitcoin mining pool finds just one block in a week as shutdown nears
items.summary: The exchange's once significant mining operation has nearly disappeared from Bitcoin's block-production rankings ahead of its November 10 closure.

items.title: Bitcoin drops, then pops as Nvidia cheating scandal and failed Iran talks trigger volatility
items.summary: Volatile price action has once again liquidated leveraged bullish plays worth millions.

items.title: What the election results mean for crypto: State of Crypto
items.summary: Democrats had an astoundingly good night, smashing all expectations. Is that actually bad news for the industry?

items.title: Stablecoin growth has stalled. The payments boom hasn't
items.summary: Stablecoin supply has barely grown this year, even as payments using the tokens surge. Circle's latest earnings offer another example of the divergence between dollars outstanding and activity on blockchain networks.

items.title: These Finland homes get free heat from bitcoin miners (as long as BTC stays above $70,000)
items.summary: A Finnish startup has 30 bitcoin mining systems working as central heating, and at today’s prices each one earns slightly more than the electricity it burns.

items.title: Binance users in some European countries told to pull crypto before fees kick in, with accounts closing by year end
items.summary: Affected accounts are reportedly set to close on Dec. 31. Users in Spain, France, and Poland say they've received similar notices.

items.title: U.S. Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC over $16 billion in alleged illicit flows
items.summary: Treasury billed the move as part of its campaign against Iran, but the order rests on MEXC's alleged role in Russian illicit finance.

items.title: EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities
items.summary: Applications close Nov. 27 for an industry group that aims to draft initial standards for holding and settling tokenized securities by early 2028.

items.title: Coinbase’s US national trust bank charter takes effect
items.summary: Coinbase plans to expand its institutional crypto custody business under the federal charter and is exploring digital asset payment products.

items.title: Robinhood opens access to US IPOs for UK retail investors
items.summary: Robinhood’s UK customers can request shares in eligible US initial public offerings at the offer price before the stocks begin trading.

items.title: BTC price eyes $73K amid Nvidia volatility: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
items.summary: Bitcoin price action fell to its lowest levels since mid-August as Nvidia reports added to sell-side pressure across stock-market futures.

items.title: Binance, Tether and Trump crypto firms face Senate records deadline
items.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal asked four crypto firms to start sending records by Nov. 30 and warned of further action if they miss the Jan. 4 deadline.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.3B in biggest weekly outflow since late June
items.summary: Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off.

items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade
items.summary: The proposed reduction aims to shorten transaction confirmation times and improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps.

items.title: tBTC bridge partially resumes as $120M Aave reserve remains frozen
items.summary: Threshold halted its tBTC bridge on Oct. 30 as operators addressed a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that could allow attackers to execute code on unpatched servers.

items.title: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest
items.summary: Vitalik Buterin wants Ethereum to embrace a store of value narrative, upsetting Bitcoin maxis. The crypto industry faces an uncertain future following the US elections.

items.title: Coinbase Joins Circle, Ripple With Final OCC Approval for Federal Trust Bank Charter
items.summary: The exchange will move its institutional crypto custody business under federal oversight, building on its 2018 New York trust charter.

items.title: Trump Says He Knows 'Nothing' About World Liberty Financial as He Defends UAE Ties
items.summary: Pressed on why he doesn't divest from the family's crypto venture, Trump said his sons run the business and every president faces conflicts.

items.title: Nvidia Board Investigates Jensen Huang After Report He Was Target of Chinese Spy Effort
items.summary: Huang told staff he had been "unfaithful" to his wife, as Nvidia shares fell nearly 5% in premarket trading on Monday.

items.title: This Bitcoin Developer’s Idea Would Make Quantum Attacks a Losing Bet
items.summary: Cory Fields wants future quantum attackers to post Bitcoin as collateral before touching vulnerable wallets, giving prepared owners a chance to recover their coins and collect a potentially costly penalty.

items.title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
items.summary: Apple and Meta’s objections mean all seven of the biggest U.S. tech companies have now asked to keep their shares off the planned OKX-ICE venue.

items.title: AI Chip Stocks Bounce After Global Rout—But Is the Bubble Starting to Burst?
items.summary: A Friday rebound offered relief after a historic selloff. The question now is whether politics and mounting debt could turn an AI correction into something much worse.

items.title: Sony Axing Game Discs Will Have Outsized Impact on Low-Income Gamers, Experts Say
items.summary: Experts say a disc-free PlayStation will price out low-income players, while in much of Africa, digital-only gaming means breaking Sony’s rules.

items.title: Treasury Cuts Crypto Exchange MEXC Off From US Financial System
items.summary: FinCEN’s order, part of Operation Economic Outcast, bars U.S. institutions from any transfers to or from MEXC, which Treasury says facilitated $16 billion in illicit finance tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia.

items.title: Greece Passes Crypto Tax Law With 10% Gains Levy, 15% on Staking and DeFi
items.summary: Greece has approved a crypto tax framework with a €500 ($557) annual gains threshold and new rules for staking and DeFi income, but lawmakers left important questions about token swaps unresolved.

items.title: Why a Hyperliquid Treasury Firm Wants to Become a US Futures Broker
items.summary: Hyperliquid Strategies has applied to become a U.S. futures commission merchant, a move that could let Americans trade perpetual futures on permissioned Hyperliquid markets, pending regulatory approval.
